messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE | sev=high | customer=ConcordHealth | reason=streaming p99 spike + dropped frames observed on single-tenant cluster r-72 | runbook=/runbooks/streaming-tail.md | thread=1778880000
oncall-alex: picking this up — oncall for tonight. :ambulance: any immediate impact on customer-facing requests?
support-claudia: Concord Ops reports user-facing timeouts in chat UI, several dropped streams, p99 ~ 6.2s (normal ~0.8s). They say it started ~15m ago.
sre-matt: adding initial metrics — across r-72: overall p95 up 3x, p99 up 7x. Streaming stalls correlate with high concurrency on a small subset of sessions from Concord (single-tenant).
engr-lina: I see a prompt pattern in request logs: a recurring nested JSON blob repeated inside user messages (~3-5MB flattened) causing long prefix processing + lots of KV cache churn. sample prompt snippet: `{"events": [{"type":"log","payload":"...[REDACTED]..."}]}` repeated 8x.
engr-lina: logs: ```[r-72] stream-serve: recv req id=cb-8921 prefix_len=5400 tokens | kv_hits=0 kv_evictions=12 tail_ms=6100```
oncall-alex: so single-tenant hot prefix + high concurrency -> lots of KV eviction which cascades to recompute, makes sense. Temporary mitigation ideas?
sre-matt: immediate: enable per-customer prefix cache pinning and increase kvcache size for r-72 (config change). Also route Concord to the smaller quantized model variant for streaming fallback to reduce compute per-token while we stabilize.
pm-aaron: Agree. We need to avoid degrading other tenants; prefer route only Concord cluster. Also inform Concord of planned short change.
support-claudia: I messaged Concord Ops (Beth) — they asked for ETA and whether this is an internal fix we can apply without app changes.
customer-ops-beth: Confirmed — they can accept a model-variant fallback for 30 minutes if it helps. Please provide status updates.
engr-lina: Executing kvcache scaling now: ```kubectl -n r-72 scale statefulset/kvcache --replicas=4 && curl -X POST https://admin.internal/kvcache/r-72/size -d 'size_mb=2048'```
engr-lina: scaled kvcache and bumped size. Observing immediate drop in kv_evictions count. :thumbsup:
sre-matt: rolling routing change to route Concord traffic to model=x86-quant-v2 (compatible with streaming) with automatic fallback disabled for 15m: ```routes apply --cluster r-72 --selector customer=concord --route model=x86-quant-v2 --timeout 15m```
oncall-alex: applied. Starting to see p99 drop: 6.2s -> 2.1s within 3m. Still above SLO but improving.
support-claudia: Concord seeing fewer UI timeouts; they reported intermittent long frames only.
engr-lina: There's still a tail from sessions where the prompt contains many code fences. Hypothesis: repeated long bracketed blocks cause repeated KV mismatches (prefix canonicalization different per block) — we should canonicalize on ingest.
pm-aaron: Longer-term: add prompt canonicalization and prefix-hashing for single-tenant customers to reduce KVC miss churn. Short-term: can we apply a request-level token cap or warn users?
sre-matt: We can enforce a soft token cap at the gateway for Concord sessions: 6k tokens. Implementing now with a 429 for over-limit or truncated streaming if allowed. Command: ```gateway update-limit --customer concord --token-cap 6000 --mode soft```
sre-matt: limit in place. We'll notify support then lift if unnecessary after analysis.
oncall-alex: good. Also enabling temporary autoscale of dedicated GPUs on r-72 to handle concurrency burst. ```infra autoscale --cluster r-72 --delta-gpu 2 --min=2 --max=8 --ttl=20m```
incident-bot: Note: autoscale event triggered by alex (manual) — reason: emergency mitigation.
sre-matt: After autoscale and routing + kvcache bump + token cap, p99 is now ~900ms for most sessions, but there are still 2% of streams with intermittent >2s tail likely tied to session churn and long-running prefixes.
customer-ops-beth: Concord thanks the team, UI has stabilized a lot. They want a short post-incident note and confirmation we won't flip them to a different model without notice.
support-claudia: noted. We'll keep Concord on the quantized variant for 30m as agreed and send a status update.
pm-aaron: Oncall handoff in 30m to next shift: please include the follow-ups: 1) run prompt canonicalization experiment for Concord traffic, 2) look at KVC hit pattern per prompt hash, 3) review autoscale events for cost impact.
oncall-alex: I'll draft a short Handoff message: current state: mitigated (p99 within 2x SLO), Concord on quantized fallback, token cap 6k enforced, kvcache increased, autoscale +2 GPUs with 20m TTL. Open action items assigned to eng-lina/sre-matt.
engr-lina: quick debug note: found a small bug in kvcache keying for multiline code fences that caused different keys for same logical prefix when original had trailing spaces. Patch PR: https://git.internal/r/patches/1234 - will backport to release-2.1 and can be hotfixed if needed.
sre-matt: Recommend hotpatch to r-72. If we do, coordinate a brief rolling restart for kvcache pods after hours or with cordon.
oncall-alex: do the hotpatch if patch validated in canary. Who owns? Lina + Matt?
engr-lina: I'll validate in staging and then cut a canary onto one kvcache pod in r-72. ETA 45m.
support-claudia: I'll tell Concord the plan and ask for permission for a short canary restart window; they said okay as long as it's <10m.
pm-aaron: Great. Oncall handoff at 1778881800. Alex, please post a summary for next shift and tag postmortem owners.
oncall-alex: Handoff summary (to be posted): "Mitigation applied: kvcache scaled & size increased; routing to quantized model for Concord; gateway soft token cap 6000; autoscale +2 GPUs TTL20m. Observed p99 back to ~900ms, customer reports stabilized. Action items: prompt canonicalization experiment (eng-lina), kvcache keying fix + canary (eng-lina + sre-matt), follow-up postmortem and billing impact assessment (pm-aaron)."
incident-bot: Incident state change: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to medium.
oncall-alex: tagging for handoff @oncall-next. I'll update if canary finds regression. :eyes:
engr-lina: canary running now on one pod; monitoring for kv_evictions and tail samples.
sre-matt: watching metrics — canary pod shows canonical keying reduces evictions by ~80% for repeated fence prompts in staging. Good signal.
oncall-alex: thanks team. I'll leave this thread open for postmortem notes. Moving to monitoring state.
support-claudia: will send customer update and close loop.
customer-ops-beth: Thanks all — Concord grateful for fast response. Please include a short summary and planned improvements.
noncall-alex: closing active mitigation. next steps: schedule postmortem, estimate cost impact of autoscale and quantized routing, and roll out canonicalization to production in controlled canary. If anything regresses, re-open thread.
incident-bot: Incident closed for paging (manual) at 1778883600 — final state: monitoring.
